statement: Suppose E[2] is irreducible. (i) On matching BU , coefficient 1 of a product of root traces reads A on the union of U and those roots. It depends on the roots only through their total rational elementary label relative to S ∪ U. Any finite collection of roots, including the empty collection, may be replaced in this test by one virtual root with that label. (ii) Changing the Legendre bit of that root against a split vertex p has additive derivative equal to deletion of p, with its rational labels away from p transferred to the total root label. Changing the root bit against a simple vertex has derivative zero. 33 (iii) To vary a simple vertex q, omit it and use opposite BV , retaining the other root probes. At another simple vertex p, choose Frobenius lifts g and ϕp for q and p. If their transposition images are different, the derivative under g 7→ gτp deletes both p and q and transfers their rational labels to the root total. If their transposition images are equal, the derivative is zero. (iv) In the test in (iii), variation at a split p is given by the first-shell factors cp times symbols of merged configurations whose weight is one less. It consequently vanishes whenever all symbols of that lower weight vanish. All these assertions preserve every specified label at the other vertices, and use the chosen place for inertia and Frobenius.
